svg.text: Subscribers keep their sessions (clean start off, no expiry), so a broker with storage keeps each QoS 1/2 message. Stores on an SSD (XFS): a synced 4 KiB write takes 0.7 ms into allocated blocks, 1.8 ms when it extends a file.
Each broker runs its most durable setting. Most send the PUBACK before the write is synced: COMPARISONS.md says which wait.
A fresh broker and store per cell. 1 s warmup, then 5 s. QoS 1/2 publishers keep 100 in flight. Broker on CPUs 0-3, with the stores it needs; its CPU sums them.
Time to PUBACK: one QoS 1 publish in flight, from its send to its PUBACK.
MQTT brokers with storage on, TCP loopback
Intel Core i7-8700B @ 3.20 GHz (QEMU/KVM), performance governor, turbo off
16 pairs: 16 publishers → 16 subscribers, a topic each
time to PUBACK, 1 QoS 1 message in flight: p99, whiskers p50 to p99.9
